To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CPB causes gut ischemia and reperfusion injury, and that the gut is an endocrine organ that produces inflammatory mediators that may contribute to the development of SIRS and MODS.
the gut is an important source of inflammatory mediators during and after CPB and that gut-derived mediators contribute to the inflammatory response in the lungs, liver, and systemic circulation.
the splanchnicrovascular response to CPB is a major contributor to postoperative organ failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the splanchno-cardio-respiratory axis in CPB.
the splanchnics and the systemic inflammatory response to CPB.
the splanchnics as a source of inflammatory mediators in the postoperative period, and with the gut as an organ vulnerable to damage during CPB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the splanchnics are a major source of inflammatory mediators and a target for injury, but the precise mechanisms and their significance remain to be determined.
CPB causes systemic inflammatory response and that the splanchnics is the most important source of the inflammatory mediators.
, in the majority of cases of CPB, the splanchnicroperfusion is inadequate and that this is a major cause of the inflammatory response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut is a major source of inflammatory mediators in CPB.
the gut, as a major source of inflammatory mediators, is the key to understanding the systemic inflammatory response to CPB.
the systemic inflammatory response to CPB is mediated by gut-derived inflammatory mediators and that the gut is a major target organ of injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut is a source of inflammatory mediators in the systemic circulation, and that these mediators are increased in the systemic circulation after CPB.
the splanchnicrovascular bed is not a passive bystander during CPB but is an active participant in the inflammatory process.
, although the systemic inflammatory response is not always clinically apparent, it does occur and is associated with splanchnic injury.
